solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

R059-01.notes: P4 'Its geometry is exact... What is conventional is the decision...' and closing 'precise solution... quiet redefinition'. A is the 'familiar telling' the author calls incomplete. B contradicted by 'None of this makes perspective arbitrary.' D: passage never attributes perspective's success to the demo's realism; too narrow and unsupported.

R059-02.notes: P2 gives 'the familiar telling'; P3 opens 'not false, but it is incomplete.' B is P4 content. C is P1 content. D: no claim Alberti misunderstood anything.

R059-03.notes: P4: medieval painters 'were not failing to see; they were answering a different question, about importance or about what a viewer needed to know.' A is the view rejected. B overstates; author doesn't rank accuracy. C unsupported/absurd; enlarging was deliberate.

R059-04.notes: P3: 'revealing precisely because it enforces those assumptions. The illusion succeeds only when the viewer is made to see as the system requires.' A: comparison happens in P1 but isn't the reason given. C: no Brunelleschi-vs-Alberti comparison. D: mirror is part of viewing setup, not correcting a flaw.

R059-05.notes: 'a neutral record' contrasted with 'a particular way of conceiving the world' -> free of a particular point of view. A (electrical), B (political), D (color) are other dictionary senses that don't fit.

R059-06.notes: P3 lists 'a single eye rather than two, an eye that does not move, and a visual field that is flat rather than curved.' A combines first two. B: Brunelleschi stood in cathedral doorway; not an assumption. C inverts flat/curved (and conflates picture with visual field). D: mirror is the demo setup, not a system assumption.

R059-07.notes: Near-paraphrase of 'Its geometry is exact... What is conventional is the decision to treat that single, motionless eye as the standard of truth.' A denies the conventional part. C makes the geometry conventional, contrary to passage; medieval methods not called exact. D: no painters-vs-scientists claim.

R059-08.notes: P5: 'conventions, once learned, become invisible'; such a viewer 'is judging it by rules that were themselves invented.' A contradicts 'not failing to see.' B: modern viewer uses perspective rules, not 14th-c standards. C: viewer isn't rejecting the geometry; if anything relies on it.

R059-09.notes: Closing: 'a precise solution to a problem of projection, and a quiet redefinition of what a picture is for'; P3 notes assumptions it enforces. B: author says 'none of this makes perspective arbitrary'; not dismissive. C: author calls the 'how vision works' telling incomplete. D: the lost painting is a factual aside, author clearly engaged.

R059-10.notes: P2: Alberti 'describing the picture as a window through which the viewer looks at the scene.' A: mirror is Brunelleschi's demo. C: Panofsky's 'symbolic form' idea, applied to perspective not Alberti's definition. D: P4's description of medieval painters' purpose.
